title: DST boundary: fix out-of-order streaming events causing per-customer quota bleed and console chart anomalies
creator: Daniel Kim
description: We are observing customers hitting unexpected quota exhaustion around daylight savings time (DST) boundaries in certain regions. Investigation shows an increase in out-of-order streaming ingest events where event_time and ingest_time cross DST offsets, causing the quota ledger to apply tokens to the wrong hourly buckets and the console per-model breakdown charts to spike. This leads to temporary negative remaining_quota values, automated retries that accelerate consumption (quota bleed), and confusing spikes in internal and customer-facing dashboards.
reproduction_steps: 1) Pick a customer with steady streaming traffic and a region that recently had a DST shift (e.g., Europe/Paris).
2) Replay a subset of production events with event_time stamped just before the DST forward/back transition and ingest_time after the transition (simulate clock offset).
3) Observe ledger writes: tokens attributed to previous hour buckets and new ingest records appended causing per-hour totals to exceed expected counts.
4) Open Console > Usage > Per-model breakdown and notice spike rows for the affected customer and model; remaining_quota shows negative seconds for short windows.
5) Trigger client retries that do not honor eventual consistency window; confirm accelerated token consumption and improper rate-limiter decisions.
proposed_solution: A) Introduce an ingestion watermarking policy: delay finalable attribution for events with event_time/injest_time delta > 2 minutes by writing to a staging TTL partition and only commit to ledger after watermark passes (configurable per-tenant).

B) Modify quota ledger to be idempotent on event_id and to support out-of-order reconciliation: keep a short-lived correction log that can move counts between hourly buckets without double-counting or leaving negative residuals.
C) Update rate-limiter to consult 'committed_watermark' for a customer when deciding enforcement within recently transitioned windows to avoid premature hard failures that trigger aggressive retries.
D) Add an automated compensating credits job to reconcile customers who experienced negative remaining_quota due to this issue and surface audit entries in the Console.
E) Add a Console annotation and chart overlay for DST transitions and ingest watermarks so SREs/PMs can correlate anomalies with timezone events.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Replayed out-of-order DST transition events do not create negative remaining_quota; per-hour ledger totals converge after watermark window without double-counting.
2) Console per-model breakdown charts show a single reconciled spike with provenance metadata instead of duplicated spikes across adjacent hours.
3) Rate-limiter no longer issues hard failures during the watermark window for affected customers; overall customer latency does not regress by >5% in sLO tests.
4) Compensating credits run produces an auditable report and customer-facing notification template for affected tenants.
5) Unit and integration tests cover idempotent ledger writes, watermark progression, and rate-limiter behavior for out-of-order events.
notes: Root cause appears to be a combination of (1) ingestion pipeline that uses event_time for bucketing but writes based on ingest_time without atomic reattribute transactions, and (2) a rate-limiter that makes enforcement decisions against a window that can be retroactively changed.
This intersects with existing DST/timezone logic; we should avoid broad timezone rewrites and instead apply a narrowly scoped watermarking + idempotency fix.

Edge-case: customers with aggressive low-latency SLAs might be sensitive to added watermark delay; make watermark window configurable by tenant tier (e.g., Dedicated customers can choose smaller window).
